$comment: THE BUILD DAG, AS DATA. One source of truth for how every image in this repo
is built, in what order, with which build args, what verifies it, and whether
CI builds and/or publishes it.
Consumed by BOTH scripts/build.sh (build order + build args + verify) and
.github/workflows/image-build.yml (matrix fan-out + published set), via
scripts/graph.sh. Before this file those two carried the same knowledge in two
hand-maintained forms -- a bash case statement and a hardcoded `for image in
...` list in the workflow -- and they had already drifted (the workflow's
published set and build.sh's `all` disagreed about the test probes).
NOT to be confused with quasar-manifest.json, which is the CATALOG contract the
Quasar control plane fetches. This file is internal build metadata; nothing
outside this repo reads it.
ADDING AN IMAGE: add an entry here and a Dockerfile. Nothing else. See
AGENTS.md, 'Adding a new image'.
ARG RESOLVERS (the value of each entry in `args`):
@version        -> the contents of ./VERSION
@tag:<image>    -> <image>:$QUASAR_IMAGE_TAG (a sibling image in this graph)
@env:NAME=DFLT  -> $NAME, or DFLT when unset/empty
anything else   -> a literal
FIELDS:
name        image name; tagged <name>:$QUASAR_IMAGE_TAG (default :dev)
dockerfile  path, built with the repo root as context
target      optional --target for a multi-stage Dockerfile
needs       sibling images that must be built first (the DAG edges)
tier        spine | leaf | artifact -- see below
args        build args, resolved as above
verify      scripts run after this image builds (build.sh verify <name>)
ci          built by GitHub Actions at all
publish     pushed to ghcr.io/<owner>/<name> on a publishing event
notes       why any of the above is the way it is
TIERS. `spine` is the shared ancestry every leaf inherits; CI builds the spine
in one sequential job FIRST so its layers are in the shared registry cache
before the leaves fan out in parallel. Without that ordering N parallel leaf
jobs each rebuild quasar-base+quasar-app from cold. `artifact` is a publishable
non-image byproduct (see the kwin RPMs).

images.name: quasar-kwin-rpms
images.notes: FROM scratch, ~12 MB: the patched-KWin RPMs and nothing else. Published under its own content-addressed tag by the kwin-artifact CI job, not by the ordinary publish path -- which is why publish=false here and why tier=artifact keeps it out of the `all` and `ci` sets (quasar-kde can also build it inline, and building it twice is 54 minutes). quasar-kde consumes it via KWIN_RPMS_IMAGE.

images.name: quasar-steam-runtime
images.notes: Two images build on this (quasar-steam, quasar-kde) and it carries the ~1.5 GB Steam/32-bit closure plus a bwrap source build, so it is spine rather than leaf: paying for it twice in parallel leaf jobs is the single largest avoidable duplicate in a fan-out.

images.name: quasar-kde
images.notes: KWIN_RPMS_IMAGE=kwin-rpms names the LOCAL stage in the same Dockerfile, i.e. build the RPMs here (~27 min). CI points it at the published quasar-kwin-rpms artefact instead.

images.name: quasar-xfce
images.notes: The X11 sibling of quasar-kde: an XFCE 4 session on a rootful Xwayland nested under the Quasar compositor, since there is no Wayland XFCE session. No KWIN_RPMS_IMAGE equivalent -- xfwm4 is the stock distro build, so this leaf is an ordinary FROM quasar-steam-runtime with no artefact dependency. publish=true states the intent; nothing on develop publishes (see the workflow's PUBLISHING MODEL), and the first real publish is the operator-gated stable batch that must ALSO add the xfce-desktop entry to quasar-manifest.json -- a published image with no catalog entry is one the control plane cannot launch.

images.name: quasar-benchapp
images.notes: kind=template in quasar-manifest.json, so nothing pulls it from a registry -- built and VERIFIED in CI (verify-benchapp.sh, which nothing ran before), not published. BENCHAPP_SRC_IMAGE is left empty here on purpose: scripts/build.sh resolves it (explicit override > a local quasar-benchapp:src > the registry image quasar-mark publishes). See AGENTS.md, 'The benchapp payload'.

images.name: quasar-test-vulkan
images.notes: Local-only GPU probe. Kept in CI because it is a COPY and a chmod on top of quasar-app -- seconds once the spine is cached -- and it is the cheapest way to notice that quasar-app stopped building. Never published: nothing consumes it from a registry.

images.name: quasar-test-egl
images.notes: Same as quasar-test-vulkan, plus one mesa-demos install.

images.name: quasar-unigine
images.notes: ci=false DELIBERATELY. It pulls 1.9 GB of EULA'd UNIGINE installers from assets.unigine.com and is never published (README: 'deliberately not published to GHCR' -- it redistributes third-party binaries). CI would therefore spend the download and the disk on an image it can neither publish nor hand to anyone. It stays in `build.sh all` for local/devbox builds, where the BuildKit cache mount makes the download a one-off.
